# Themes

<Lead>
A theme sets the whole look: color, type, corners and light. Clawscale ships two themes, and each has a light and a dark color scheme. Components never need to know which one is active.
</Lead>

| Theme | Look |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | Calm and neutral, for tools people use all day. Inter, rounded corners, blue accents. |
| `futuristic` | A heads-up display for mission control. Oxanium, cut corners, cyan light and glowing readouts. |

<Example name="guides/themes/preview" align="start">
  <ThemesPreview />
</Example>

## Use the futuristic theme

Load its stylesheet after the main one.

```tsx
import "@clawscale/react/styles.css";
import "@clawscale/react/themes/futuristic.css";
import "@clawscale/react/fonts.css";
```

Pick it on the provider, and pass the same default to `ThemeScript` so the first paint matches.

```tsx
<ClawscaleProvider defaultTheme="futuristic">{children}</ClawscaleProvider>
```

```tsx
<ThemeScript defaultTheme="futuristic" />
```

Without its stylesheet, a theme falls back to the default look, and the provider logs a warning.

## Let people choose

`useTheme` returns the theme and a setter. The choice is saved, like the color scheme. This picker changes the theme of these docs. So does Shift + T.

<Example name="guides/themes/picker">
  <ThemesPicker />
</Example>

## What the futuristic theme changes

- **Type.** Oxanium for text and JetBrains Mono for numbers, breadcrumbs and tooltips. Buttons, tabs, column headers and section titles are set in capitals.
- **Data keeps its case.** Tags, inputs, menu items, table cells and buttons that open a menu or a select never change case.
- **Shape.** Corners are cut, not rounded. Radios, slider handles and switch knobs become diamonds.
- **Light.** Primary actions, focus, the selected tab and metrics glow in the dark color scheme. The light color scheme draws crisp lines instead.
- **Surfaces.** A faint grid on the page, a lit edge on cards, callouts and toasts, and progress bars that fill in segments.
- **Color.** Luminous intent fills with dark text in the dark color scheme. Every text and intent color passes WCAG AA, as in the default theme.

### Intents

Each swatch shows the light color scheme on the left and the dark one on the right.

<ColorSwatches group="intents" theme="futuristic" />

### Chart palette

Eight slots, in the same fixed order in both color schemes. Neighboring slots stay distinct for color-blind readers. In the light color scheme, slot 6 falls below 3:1 contrast on the surface, so label that series directly or offer a table.

<ChartSwatches theme="futuristic" />

Chart libraries that take an array can use `chartPalettes.futuristic`. See [Charts](/docs/patterns/charts/).

## Themes and color schemes

The theme and the color scheme are separate settings. `colorScheme` picks light, dark or system for any theme. See [Clawscale provider](/docs/core/clawscale-provider/).

| Attribute on `<html>` | Values |
| --- | --- |
| `data-cs-theme` | `default`, `futuristic` or the name of your own theme |
| `data-cs-color-scheme` | `light` or `dark` |

## Scope a theme

Set `data-cs-theme` on any element to give its subtree another theme, and `data-cs-color-scheme` for another color scheme. Both nest, and the closest one wins. The preview above shows both themes on one page.

```tsx
<Card data-cs-theme="futuristic">...</Card>
```

Overlays render in a portal on `<body>`, so they take the page's theme. Inside a scoped subtree, render them in place with `usePortal={false}`.

## Browser support

The futuristic theme uses `corner-shape`, `@scope` and `light-dark()`.

- Browsers without `corner-shape` keep small rounded corners.
- Browsers without `@scope` get the theme's tokens: its colors, fonts, corners and capital labels. They skip its glows, grid and panel accents.

## Build your own theme

A theme is data: a `ThemeDefinition` from `@clawscale/tokens` with shared tokens, a light and a dark color scheme and a sequential ramp. Start from a built-in theme, render its CSS with `renderThemeCss` and load the file after the Clawscale styles.

```ts
import { renderThemeCss, type ThemeDefinition, themes } from "@clawscale/tokens";

const base = themes.default;

export const harbor: ThemeDefinition = {
  ...base,
  name: "harbor",
  label: "Harbor",
  description: "The default theme with teal accents.",
  light: { ...base.light, color: { ...base.light.color, primary: "#0E7C6B", "primary-text": "#0B6B5C" } },
  dark: { ...base.dark, color: { ...base.dark.color, primary: "#0E7C6B", "primary-text": "#4FD1B8" } },
};

// At build time, write the CSS and load it after @clawscale/react/styles.css.
const css = renderThemeCss(harbor);
```

Then pass `defaultTheme="harbor"`. Check every text and intent color with `contrastRatio` from `@clawscale/tokens`, as Clawscale's own tests do.
